summary: Documented a false positive in the /codeyam-audit presentability pass: glob-loaded content collections are reached through getCollection(), never by an import of the entry's path, so the scan's 'unreferenced' test can flag live content as deletion candidates. The procedure now names the mechanism, records that the finding is unstable, and gives a one-command way to check any flagged path before acting on it.

changes.title: GOTCHA: glob-loaded content can be reported as a stale doc
changes.description: The presentability scan finds stale docs by asking which tracked files no other tracked file references. Content collections are discovered by a directory glob and reached via getCollection('<name>'), so nothing references them the way the scan means, and they can be listed as deletion candidates — acting on that deletes live site content. The GOTCHA states the mechanism, prescribes checking the content config for a glob loader whose base covers the flagged path, and deliberately points at stack.json's data.contentDir rather than hardcoding src/content, since assuming that path is the same mistake the underlying bug makes. It also warns that the count is not trustworthy in either direction: across one day on this repo the same 8 unchanged event entries were reported as 1 candidate, then 8, then none, with no change to the content, the content config, or the dependency graph, and a full analyze-imports rebuild did not bring the finding back. So a clean scan is not evidence the class is gone. That instability is deliberately left as an open observation rather than explained, because I could not reproduce the flip.

waysToTest.text: Read the GOTCHA block under section 6 of .claude/skills/codeyam-audit/finalize-procedure.md — the prose is the entire change. There is no executable surface, so no test can be red against it.
Exercise the check it prescribes: grep -nE "glob\(|base:" src/content/config.ts prints the loader bases, including ${root}/events — which is what proves the event entries are live rather than dead.

See the instability the GOTCHA warns about: grep -n "stale-doc candidate" .codeyam/logs/session-finalize.log shows the count reported as 1 on six runs then 8 on two, while codeyam-editor editor presentability-scan currently reports none — same 8 files on disk throughout.
